original_title: TagTinker Lets You Hack Electronic Shelf Labels
original_content:
Was there ever anything wrong with simple paper price labels? Absolutely not. And yet, the world invented the electronic price tag anyway. If you happen to come across some of these devices and want to hack them, you might like TagTinker from [i12bp8].
TagTinker is a Flipper Zero application specifically built for talking to infrared electronic shelf labels (ESLs). These are e-paper devices that receive commands and updates via an infrared interface, and theyre relatively simple to talk to. [i12bp8] built upon previous work from [furrtek] which revealed the protocols used to update these devices, and implemented it into an app that runs on the Flipper. It can do neat things like scan the NFC tags built into ESLs to ID them, deploy bitmap images to the tags, or run live-updated dashboards on the devices with the aid of a Flipper WiFi devboard.
If youve always wanted to play with these tags but didnt want to do the grunt work yourself, it just got a whole lot easier to mess around. Though, its worth noting, [i12bp8] has strictly prohibited any illegal uses of this app, so be good out there. Weve seen these tags repurposed before, too  who knew they could make such good conference badges?
